text: The aisle smelled of floor wax and ripe bananas, a scent that transported Mrs. Gable straight back to the chalk dust of Room 304. She was reaching for a tin of peaches when a hand brushed hers—not aggressively, but with a hesitation she recognized instantly. It was Leo, now broad-shouldered and graying at the temples, holding a basket full of organic kale. He didn’t say *hello*; he said, "Mrs. Gable," the way he used to answer roll call, voice dropping an octave in respect. She smiled, letting go of the peaches so he could take them instead, a small surrender of authority that felt, after twenty years, like the only lesson that had ever truly stuck.
